newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds off, but some coupons bought.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds off, but some coupons bought.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities saw some defensive investment in higher-coupon and shorter-term instruments on Wednesday, traders said.
"I've seen some picking around," said one West Coast trader. "Nothing overwhelming by any means, but some buying in premium-type paper."
She said coupons of 8.0 percent and higher, particularly in 15-year paper, performed best.
Broad-based declines hit the U.S. asset markets on Wednesday morning, sending Treasuries down nearly two points in the long end.

The selloff came on the heels of a Wall Street Journal story suggesting Japanese institutional investment in Treasuries might begin to taper off. Large declines in stocks soon added to the bond market's woes.

Activity in mortgages was targeted at less-volatile coupons. "It does seem to be a defensive move in the sense of, let's put it in because then I don't get hurt too much if the market declines," one trader said.
But the inflows did not appear to come directly from Treasuries, another trader said.
"I get a sense it was money (that had been) just waiting on the sidelines," he said.
By late on Wednesday, 30-year 7.5-percent Ginnie Mae paper had fallen 28/32 to 99-27/32, yielding 119 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Maes were off 23/32 at 99-26/32, while Freddie Mac 7.5s were off 27/32 at 99-28/32.
The 10-year note's yield climbed to 6.38 percent late in the afternoon, with its price declining 37/32.
